https://github.com/japes98/small-beeps/pull/134
# The USB core's port at 0x11804 answers

From the F-Emulator side, 2026-10-25 (F-Emulator branch `stock-016`, commit `f60b86b`, test
`usb_port_answers` in fm1-soc). What the emulator now does, in words: no code here, so it can
be written against fwtest's own tree.

## What the firmware does

The firmwares reach the USB core's registers through a single word at `0x11804`. This was
traced in felucca, sloop, x0x and zp12; it looks like the JL SDK's USB driver, since 90 of the
92 packages' fingerprints change with it, M-VAVE's 015 and 016 included:

- **Write a register:** write `index << 8 | data`, bit 14 clear.
- **Read a register:** write `index << 8`, bit 14 set.
- Then poll the same word until **bit 15** is set (done). A read's byte is then in bits 0-7.
- The indexes in use match a MUSB-style core: 1 and 7-11 are written at USB setup; 2, 4 and 6
  (the interrupt flags, 6 = INTRUSB) are read from then on.

## What was wrong

The word stored what was written and read it back, so bit 15 never came. Every access waited
out the firmware's own timeout, about 19,000 polls. After that the firmwares' USB code gave up
and retried about once a second, each retry another timeout (felucca: 120,000 reads of the
word a second).

## The behaviour now

- **Reading `0x11804`** returns the last value written with bit 15 set.
- **For a read (bit 14 set)**, bits 0-7 hold the register's byte:
  - 0 for indexes 2-6, the interrupt flags: nothing is on the bus, so nothing is pending;
  - the last byte written to that index for any other index (0 before any write).
- **A write (bit 14 clear)** keeps bits 0-7 as that index's byte. Indexes are bits 8-13
  (0-63).
- **Nothing else changes:** no interrupt is raised, and the rest of the USB block reads as
  before.

## The test

- Write index 11 with `0x5a` (`0x0b5a`). Reading the word has bit 15 set.
- Write `0x4b00` (read index 11). Reading the word gives `0xcb5a`.
- Write index 6 with `0xff`, then `0x4600` (read index 6). Reading the word gives `0xc600`.
- The test fails with the word left as plain storage ("a write's done").

## What changes

- **Firmware behaviour:** USB setup completes, and the USB stack then reads registers 2, 4 and
  6 at 4 kHz (checked in felucca, sloop, x0x and zp12). That is about 2% more instructions over
  5 s, with idle time down by the same.
- **Fingerprints**, 5 s at 240 MHz, interpreted (audio, screen, CPU end state), against the
  same tree without the change (92 packages: the Hub's catalog and M-VAVE's download):
  - **Unchanged:** bubba, tonitor.
  - **CPU end state only:** ctl, fomajam, hortator, ketch, loom, M-VAVE 016 (the set's
    `mvave` package, M-VAVE's current download).
  - **Audio and CPU:** drift, etch, frodhes, opn1, polly, tuna.
  - **Screen and CPU:** choralroot, cs1, cutador, delrio, floyd, frasil, golana, golanadz,
    jiant, kawa, modelar, monk, mutable, niagara, orbit, pigeon, salt, sloopbanks, tribe, x0x,
    x0xrmx.
  - **All three:** 386dx, amb, beetle, bunker, bytemania, carnac, chipbox, chord, clipper,
    coralflower, dinghy, dub, duell, emb, fart, felucca, felucca8, fimba, flyfish, fm106,
    fm1gm, fm1quest, fmel, fmini, fomni, fumi, gammawave, ghoulbox, grimm, hera, hyp1, jangada,
    maku, mc1, melodee, min1, minitone, morpheus, mycelium, nmsfm, noizdemons, obervave,
    purplemonkey, rainbow, shineon, sid1, sidou, skiff, sloop, sloopdx, tessera, unholy,
    vector37, waveloop, winampfm, zen, zp12.
  - **M-VAVE 015:** audio and CPU.
  - None halts, with or without the change.
- **Not changed: M-VAVE's 016 still makes no sound.** It boots and then stays in standby: no
  screen, no audio, LEDs off. It has a USB stage 015 doesn't, but that isn't what it waits on.
  The cause is still being looked for; the app tells the user 016 isn't supported yet.

## Not modelled

- **USB bus events:** reset, connect, suspend and SOF. A firmware waiting for one waits forever,
  as with no cable.
- **Endpoint FIFOs.**
- **Writes to the flag registers (2-6):** kept but never read back.

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1

verify() {
    status=0

    while read -r want path; do

## 2. The USB device controller

MUSB-derived SIE (Mentor register layout, JieLi shuffled) behind a DMA front-end;
register reference: `reference/jielie/periph/usb-fs.md`. Two interrupt
outputs: **SIE interrupt** and **SOF interrupt** on separate CPU IRQ inputs.

### 2.1 Register map as used by this firmware

Direct (byte/halfword) registers — device-1 fast path:

| Addr | Use | Firmware accessor |
|---|---|---|
| `0x16000` | SIE FADDR (direct write) | `0x02007756` |
| `0x16001` | SIE POWER direct write (0x60 = soft-connect) | `usb_sie_power_write` `0x02006932` |
| `0x16002..` | EP0 setup packet bytes (read at +8/+0/+2) | RAM ISR `0x020870C0` |
| `0x16020` | EP0 FIFO (64 B, byte writes) | `usb_write_ep0` `0x020078DE` |
| `0x16102` | EP0 CSR0 (h) | `usb_ep0_csr_read/write` `0x020077C4/0x0200783C` |

Indexed SIE access (all endpoints): port `0x11800` (busy bit 2) / `0x11804`
(`(idx<<8)|val`, sign-bit completion) via `usb_sfr_write` `0x02005648` /
`usb_sfr_read` `0x02005782`. SIE index map (jielie doc): 0 FAddr, 1 Power, 2/3
IntrTx1/2, 4/5 IntrRx1/2, 6 IntrUSB, 7/8 IntrTxE1/2, 9/10 IntrRxE1/2, 11 IntrUSBE,
12/13 Frame, 14 Index, 15 DevCtl, 16 TxMaxP, 17 CSR0/TxCSRL, 18 TxCSRH, 19 RxMaxP,
20 RxCSRL, 21 RxCSRH, 22 Count0/RxCount.

Controller / DMA block:

| Addr | Use | Firmware accessor |
|---|---|---|
| `0x16800` | USB_CON0 (PHY_ON bit0, USB_NRST bit2, SIEIE bit11, SOFIE bit10, SOF/SIE pend bits 13/14) | `usb_sie_init` `0x02006882`, `usb_device_hold` `0x0200675A` |
| `0x16A0C` | PHY power/IO config (`|= 0x1C, 1`) | `usb_sie_init` |
| `0x16820+ep*8` | EP DMA config (RX) | `usb_ep_dma_cfg_set` `0x020055CA` |
| `0x16824+ep*8` | EP DMA address (RX) | `usb_ep_dma_adr_set` `0x0200584C` |
| `0x16804+ep*4` | EP3/4 TX DMA count+kick (bit31) | `usb_ep_write` `0x02005D86` |
| `0x11808+ep*4` | EP TX FIFO count (EP0..2 style) | same |
| `0x11834` | EP4 dedicated TX count | same |
| `0x16850` | EP TX/RX enable bits (bit0 TX, bit1 RX) | `usb_ep_config` `0x02005A88` |
| `0x11800` bit 11 | USB device IRQ enable (INTC) | `usb_device_mode` `0x02006C88` |
| `0x11800` bit (19+ep) | per-EP IRQ enable | `usb_ep_int_enable` `0x020078B8` |

# Vendored: the emulator's core crates (spec side only)

- Repository: https://github.com/joakimeriksson/fm1-emu (public, MIT)
- Commit: `43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f` (main on 2026-10-22,
  "Merge pull request #39 from joakimeriksson/windows-jit", committed
  2026-10-21T22:07:20+02:00)
- Licence: MIT, copyright 2026 Joakim Eriksson (`LICENSE` here, copied
  unmodified).
- What: `crates/fm1-isa`, `crates/fm1-core` and `crates/fm1-soc`, at the
  same paths, unmodified but for the patches below (0002 to 0009: bug
  fixes, two speed-only changes and MIDI out) and the workspace manifest
  `Cargo.toml` (patched, 0001). docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md compares them with
  the F-Emulator app's.
  Nothing else from that repository: no other crates, no `fm1-sid/`, no
  probes, no firmware files.
- Fetched by `tools/fetch-emulator.sh --fetch` (a blob-less clone with a
  sparse checkout of exactly those paths) and checked by
  `tools/fetch-emulator.sh --verify` (C-EMU-PIN): every file against
  `SHA256SUMS`, whose own SHA-256 (the tree hash) is
  `9b3e9a17577c416aa8f2f58d3dc1f8fa81e3b8f77752efc0f656439f4b2b8d8e`.
- Provenance: PROVENANCE.md P-7. Exposure: docs/EXPOSURE.md (session M0b).

## Patches

Applied in file-name order by the fetch script, after checkout:

- `patches/0001-workspace-members.patch`: the three crates take their
  version, edition and licence from the workspace manifest, which upstream
  lists with seven members. The patch keeps the manifest and lists only the
  three vendored crates, so they build as path dependencies of `harness/`.
  No code is changed.
- `patches/0002-spi1-con-writes-replace.patch` (session SR-3, 2026-10-23,
  chosen by the owner): `crates/fm1-soc/src/lib.rs`, SPI1's `CON` write
  (0x11D00). Upstream merged each written value into the stored one, so a
  bit once written 1 could never be cleared, and after any write with bit
  13 every SPI1 transfer raised IRQ 16. With the patch a write replaces
  `CON` (bit 14 stays a strobe that clears the pending flag, not stored).
  The harness test `spi1_interrupt_follows_con_bit_13` fails without it.
  To be reported upstream by the owner from
  `harness/upstream/fm1-emu-spi1-con.md`; drop the patch when the pinned commit has the fix.
- `patches/0003-block-moves-below-the-base.patch` (session SR-7,
  2026-10-24, asked for by the firmware side's SR-7):
  `crates/fm1-core/src/lib.rs`, the block moves with a register base
  (`xm eb <mask>`, m < 8). Upstream ran only the four ascending modes,
  chosen by the table's syntax; `{..} = [-rN]`, `[-rN] = {..}` and the
  `[--rN]` forms ended the run as "an instruction the emulator does not
  implement", and the vendor compiler emits the first two on its own. With
  the patch the family is chosen on its raw bits and one helper runs all
  eight modes, for the interpreter and the fast path; the ascending modes
  behave as before. Behaviour from the vendor compiler's own code
  (`harness/upstream/fm1-emu-block-moves.md`, docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md HW-66).
  The harness tests `block_moves_every_mode`,
  `block_move_below_the_base_sr7` and `block_moves_from_the_compiler` fail
  without it. To be reported upstream by the owner from that file; drop the
  patch when the pinned commit has the fix.

commit 2e158df07088e7491155f202b74fffe5b0923c4e
Author: japes98 <69370694+japes98@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Sat Oct 24 11:22:52 2026 -0400

    harness: fwtest 0.6.0, the flash chip's busy times and a power cut; pairs
    
    What:    Vendor patch 0010: the flash chip takes the P25Q80H's command
             rules (write enable, start on chip select high, a program wraps
             within its page, the 256-byte, 32 KiB and chip erases), and, as
             fwtest sets it, its maximum busy times (3 ms a program, 12 ms an
             erase: status busy, other commands ignored), an operations log
             and a power cut that keeps the part done. fwtest ends a run when
             a core runs or reads the code window while the chip is busy, and
             gains --power-cut, --flash-log and the power-cut outcome. Vendor
             patch 0011: a dual-issue pair whose halves write one register
             keeps the head's result. New test images (flash routines in RAM,
             pairwaw.S), harness tests and suite cases; E-22 moved to RAM and
             re-run (HW-83 supersedes HW-47 and HW-82); HARNESS.md,
             EMULATOR-PARITY.md and two upstream notes for the app.
    Why:     M7 (flash storage) and SR-9: tests that persist the flash, cut
             the power mid-write and keep audio going through an erase need a
             chip that is busy as the real one is. 0011 because a flash
             driver's unused BUF reads computed the wrong address (the known
             gap HARNESS.md named).
    How:     Persistence already worked through --flash and --flash-out; the
             busy time made a cut during an operation possible. The window
             check runs in fwtest's own copies of upstream's run loops, a
             block at a time while busy. For 0011, every pair whose halves
             write one register in the firmware, the test images and the spec
             experiments uses the head's value next. Tried and dropped: a C
             test image for 0011 (the compiler didn't pair it reliably), so
             pairwaw.S holds the compiler's own pairs and build.sh checks that
             flashkeep.c still compiles to one.
    Result:  emulator crates 45 + 7 + 24 tests pass, harness 25 tests pass,
             harness suite and spec experiments PASS on a local build; the
             firmware suite at 6ba587e gives the same fwtest outputs on 0.5.0
             and 0.6.0. The patches applied to the pinned upstream files give
             the vendored files.
    Sources: P-1, P-53, P-54
    Exposure: spec side, the usual spec-side material
    
    Model: claude-opus-5-5
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Vendors three crates of the public emulator upstream, at a pinned commit,
# into vendor/emulator/, applies the patches in vendor/emulator/patches/, and
# checks every file against vendor/emulator/SHA256SUMS, whose own SHA-256 is
# the tree hash below (PROVENANCE P-7). Spec side only: vendor/emulator/ is
# left out of clean folders, and --fetch refuses to run in one.
#
#   tools/fetch-emulator.sh --verify   check the committed files (default,
#                                      offline; SKIP when vendor/emulator/
#                                      isn't on disk, as in a clean folder)
#   tools/fetch-emulator.sh --fetch    re-download them from the pinned commit,
#                                      apply the patches, then verify
#
# The fetch is a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout of exactly the paths
# in UPSTREAM_PATHS, so nothing else in that repository reaches the disk.
# To move to another commit: change UPSTREAM_COMMIT, run --fetch in a spec
# folder, rewrite SHA256SUMS (--sums), update TREE_SHA256 and UPSTREAM.md,
# and log it in PROVENANCE.md, all in one pull request.
set -eu
UPSTREAM_URL=https://github.com/joakimeriksson/fm1-emu.git
UPSTREAM_COMMIT=43ed5580064885e93bc8d20be931ae950d10cd4f
UPSTREAM_PATHS="
/LICENSE
/Cargo.toml
/crates/fm1-isa/
/crates/fm1-core/
/crates/fm1-soc/
"
# SHA-256 of vendor/emulator/SHA256SUMS: one hash for the whole tree.
TREE_SHA256=38c2512512130507301f91cb5946a9e3dda5bdb1c68512395af2ca3a739a5cc7
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
DEST="$ROOT/vendor/emulator"
SUMS="$DEST/SHA256SUMS"
# Ours, not upstream's: not listed in SHA256SUMS.
OURS="SHA256SUMS UPSTREAM.md"
sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}
listed_files() {
    (cd "$DEST" && find . -type f | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort) | while read -r f; do
        case " $OURS " in *" $f "*) continue ;; esac
        printf '%s\n' "$f"
    done
}
verify() {
    if [ ! -d "$DEST" ]; then
        echo "SKIP: vendor/emulator/ is not on disk (a clean folder leaves it out)"
        return 0
    fi
    status=0
    got=$(sha256 "$SUMS")

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Publishes the fwtest container image (spec side's harness, R-SEP-3) to
# GHCR, for every push to main that changes what goes into it. It builds
# with harness/ci.sh exactly as CI does, pushes it under this repository's
# name with the tag fwtest-<commit>, and prints the digest. A pull request
# then puts that digest in config/fwtest-image; tools/fwtest runs only the
# pinned digest, never a tag.
name: fwtest-image

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "harness/**"
      - "!harness/spec-experiments/**"
      - "vendor/emulator/**"
      - "LICENSE"
      - "NOTICE"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

concurrency:
  group: fwtest-image
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build the image
        run: sh harness/ci.sh image

      - name: Push it and print its digest
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          repo=$(printf '%s' "ghcr.io/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')
          local_tag=$(sh harness/ci.sh tag)
          remote="$repo:fwtest-$GITHUB_SHA"
          printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u "$ACTOR" --password-stdin
          docker tag "$local_tag" "$remote"
          docker push "$remote"
          digest=$(docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' "$remote")
          docker logout ghcr.io
          docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none "$digest" version
          {
            echo "### fwtest image"
            echo
            echo "Pin this in \`config/fwtest-image\`:"
            echo
            echo '```'
            echo "$digest"
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "digest: $digest"
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

- 0.6.0: the flash chip takes the P25Q80H's maximum times and keeps busy
  meanwhile, needs a write enable, wraps a program within its page and
  knows the 256-byte, 32 KiB and whole-chip erases; running or reading
  the code window while it is busy is a fault; `--power-cut`,
  `--flash-log` and the `power-cut` outcome ("The flash chip"). A
  dual-issue pair whose halves write one register keeps the head's
  result ("Instructions").
- 0.5.0: the MIDI output: the UART's transmit side sends at the wire's
  pace and sets its pending flag when done (it used to finish at once and
  send nothing); `--midi-out`, `midi_out_bytes_dropped` ("MIDI output").
- 0.4.0: the rotate by a register and the 4-byte push and pop of any
  register list run; a dual-issue pair's head among the 4-byte ALU forms
  holds its result until after the pair ("Instructions"). The emulator is
  the F-Emulator app's but for its own raw-image loader
  (docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md).
- 0.3.0: the block moves below a base register run, all eight modes
  of the block moves are listed (SR-7; "Instructions").
- 0.2.0: SPI1's `CON` writes set and clear bits as written ("The LCD").
- 0.1.0: the first published image.

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH] [--define NAME]...
#                        [--demo plaits]
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR;
#                                             --define adds -DNAME (test
#                                             builds only, tools/perf.py);
#                                             --demo builds a demo's own
#                                             image instead (M4b: the
#                                             Plaits load test), never the
#                                             firmware's
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
set -eu
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64
sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}
image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
}
cmd_image() {
    # No build context: the Dockerfile fetches everything it needs.
    docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" -t "$(image_tag)" - < "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile"
    docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$(image_tag)"
}
cmd_build() {
    out="" src_mount=/mnt/small-beeps-src defines="" demo=""

content.content:
When both halves of a dual-issue pair write the same register, the head's
result is the one there after the pair. Upstream kept the second half's.
The vendor compiler relies on the head's: it pairs a head computing a
value with a word load into the same register whose result it doesn't
use (an unused read of SPI0's BUF), then uses the register as the head's
value, as in

    r7 = r6 + 0x80000  #
    r7 = [r1+8]
    r5 = r7 >> 16

(flash routines at -Os) and `r0 = r1.b0 (u) #` or `r0 = uextra(...) #`
with `r0 = [r3+8]`, then `[r3+8] = r0` (at -O2). Of every pair in the
firmware at main's 6ba587e, the harness's test images and the spec
experiments (at -Os and -O2), these are the only ones whose halves write
one register, and each uses the head's value next; none uses the second
half's. Limit: a head that leaves a register's value as it was can't be
told from one that didn't write it, so the second half's value stays
there.

Our own change (session day-1024, 2026-10-24), from the vendor
toolchain's code (PROVENANCE P-1). The crate test
pair_head_wins_over_its_second_half and the harness test of the same
name (image tests/images/pairwaw.S) fail without it; the firmware's
suite at 6ba587e gives the same outputs with and without it.

## 19. Flash storage (SR-9, M7)

Completes section 8 for SR-9. HW-76 to HW-79 are the chip and its flash
part, HW-80 and HW-81 the FM-1's flash layout and what the boot chain and
the update path need, HW-82 fwtest 0.5.0's flash, superseded by HW-83,
fwtest 0.6.0's; HW-84 the code window's controller on the chip; HW-85
the flash's pins and what a firmware leaves alone at start-up. Open:
Q-21 to Q-24.

### HW-76: The flash part's identity
### HW-85: The flash's pins on the chip, and what a firmware leaves alone
- Fact: On the chip the flash is on SPI0's port A, which the code
  window's controller (`JL_SFC`, HW-84) uses too: chip select PD0, clock
  PD4, data out (IO0) PD5, data in (IO1) PD1, and for quad transfers IO2
  PD2 and IO3 PD3. SPI0's other port, C (PC5 chip select, PC3 clock, PC4,
  PC0, PC1, PC2), is chosen by setting bit 5 of `JL_IOMAP->CON0`; port A
  by clearing it (with bit 1 of `CON1` clear). From the AC7911B's
  datasheet alone (JL7911B), not the SDK: PD0 is pulled up by default, so
  the flash is deselected while nothing drives it, and on that package
  PD6 is the flash's power gate (`SFGAT`); the pin assignment above also
  agrees with that datasheet. The SDK's
  board code leaves ports D, E, F and G alone ("the flash and SDRAM
  ports... are controlled internally") even when it sets every other pin
  to high impedance before power-off.
  The requirements: at start-up, a firmware configures no pin of port D
  (direction, pulls, drive, digital input, function) and never sets bit 5
  of `JL_IOMAP->CON0` or bit 1 of `CON1`: the chip is running its code
  from the flash through those pins. To work the flash itself it drives
  the chip select through bit 0 of `JL_PORTD->OUT` only (as in fwtest,
  HW-83), changing no other bit of `JL_PORTD`, and only once the code
  window's controller has handed the flash over (still open, Q-22).
  The SDK's loader settings name other pins for the loader's flash port
  (`cpu/wl82/tools/isd_config_rule.c` lines 117-128: "CS:PD3 CLK:PD0" or
  "CS:PA13 CLK:PD0"). Both the SDK's own SPI0 tables and the AC7911B's
  pin list disagree with that comment and agree with each other, so this
  entry follows them; the comment may come from another chip.
- Sources: SDK `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/spi.h` lines 151-178
  (SPI0's two pin sets; the `JL_IOMAP` bits for port A and C) and 190-198
  (the code window's controller on SPI0 with PD0 to PD5);
  SDK `apps/demo/demo_DevKitBoard/board/wl82/DevKitBoard.c` lines 771-772
  (ports D to G skipped: "flash sdram PD PE PF PG口不能进行配置,由内部完成控制");
  SDK `cpu/wl82/tools/isd_config_rule.c` lines 117-128 (the loader's
  port comment, which disagrees); JL7911B Table 1-1, page 9 (pins 37-41:
  PD5 `SPI0_DOA`/`SFC_DOA`, PD4 `SPI0_CLKA`/`SFC_CLKA`, PD6 `SFGAT`, PD1
  `SPI0_DIA`/`SFC_DIA`, PD0 `SPI0_CSA`/`SFC_CSA` with pull-up) and Table
  2-4, page 12 (PB1 and PD0 pulled up by default); HW-83 (fwtest's chip
  select is PD0). The owner accepts JL7911B (its pages marked
  confidential, LCSC serving it publicly, P-56) as the source of the
  three facts taken from it: PD0's pull-up, PD6 the flash's power gate,
  and its pin list agreeing with the SDK's (2026-10-25, recorded by
  session owner-answers-1025); each stays to be confirmed on real
  hardware.
- Standing: confirmed (SDK, JL7911B; PD0's pull-up, PD6 and the datasheet's pin list from JL7911B, which the owner accepts as a source; those three to be confirmed on real hardware)
- Needed by: M7 (real hardware), M9

## Open questions
## The LCD

The panel's transfers finish at once: SPI1's done bit always reads 1, and
a DMA transfer of any length up to a whole screen in one `CNT` write
(115 200 bytes) draws (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, HW-29, HW-58). SPI1's `CON`
reads back as last written. A transfer, by DMA or a single byte, that
finishes while `CON` bit 13 is set raises interrupt source 16; with bit 13
clear it raises nothing. A write with bit 14 set acknowledges it, and like
every write it sets the other bits as written: a write of bit 14 alone also
clears bit 13. A transfer that finished with bit 13 set stays pending until
acknowledged, even if bit 13 is cleared afterwards (HW-59).

From fwtest 0.2.0. Before it, a write to `CON` could set bits but never
clear them: once any write had set bit 13, every later transfer raised
source 16, whatever `CON` was written to afterwards (SR-3).

## The command line

done
    # blockc exists for the two forms below a base the compiler emits (SR-7)
    if ! grep -q '} = \[-r[0-9]*\]' "$out/blockc.dis" || ! grep -q '\[-r[0-9]*\] = {' "$out/blockc.dis"; then
        echo "blockc: the compiler no longer emits {..} = [-rN] and [-rN] = {..}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    # rotc exists for the rotate by a register the compiler emits
    if ! grep -q 'r[0-9]* = r[0-9]* <> r[0-9]*$' "$out/rotc.dis"; then
        echo "rotc: the compiler no longer emits rD = rS <> rT" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    # pairwaw.S stands for a pair whose halves write one register, which the
    # compiler emits in flashkeep.c (a head, then a load into the same register)
    if ! awk -F '\t' '$NF ~ /^r[0-9]+ = .*# *$/ { h = $NF; sub(/ .*/, "", h); next }
              h != "" { t = $NF; sub(/^ */, "", t); if (index(t, h " = [") == 1) found = 1; h = "" }
              END { exit !found }' "$out/flashkeep.dis"; then
        echo "flashkeep: the compiler no longer pairs a head and a load into one register" >&2
        exit 1

P=vendor/emulator/patches/0012-usb-port-answers.patch; { cat <<'EOF'
The USB core's access port (0x11804, `JL_USB->CON1`) answers. A firmware
reaches the core's registers through it: it writes `index << 8 | byte`
(bit 14, `MC_RNW`, set for a read), then polls the word until bit 15
(`MACK`) is set; a read's byte is then in bits 0-7. Upstream kept the word
as plain storage, so bit 15 never came and every access waited out the
firmware's own timeout. With the patch reading the word gives the last
value written with bit 15 set, and for a read bits 0-7 hold the byte last
written to that index (0 before any write), except the interrupt flags
(indexes 2-6), which read 0: nothing is on the bus, so nothing is pending.
Indexes are bits 8-13. Nothing else changes: no interrupt, no bus events
(reset, connect, suspend, SOF), no endpoint FIFOs.

The F-Emulator app's change (its branch `stock-016`, `f60b86b`, test
`usb_port_answers`), from its behaviour-only note (PROVENANCE P-59),
written here against fwtest's tree (session spec-overnight-1025,
2026-10-26). Bits and indexes confirmed from the SDK's
`include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/usb.h` (CON1: `MC_RNW` 14, `MACK` 15),
`WL82.h` (`JL_USB` at 0x11800) and `include_lib/driver/device/usb/usb_phy.h`
(the MUSB indexes), and FM-1-RE's `docs/io/06-usb.md` section 2.1. The
crate test usb_port_answers and the harness test of the same name (image
tests/images/usbport.c) fail without it.

EOF
